Front Matter

0.4-the-books-language 0.4-the-books-language

Engineering

**Authority.** Who is entitled to exercise engineering judgment: to decide what a system must do, permit or refuse an action, and answer for the result.

Software Agents

**Agent.** An AI system that pursues an open-ended or underspecified task through multiple steps, exercising judgment about what to do next and using tools in response to intermediate results.

MAGE

**Agentic engineering.** The engineering of systems and environments in which autonomous agents perform consequential work.

0.5-preface 0.5-preface

How do we safely grant autonomy to commodity intelligence?

This is a book about engineering: what engineering becomes when reasoning capacity becomes abundant.

MAGE: Model-Based Agentic Engineering

*Agentic engineering* is the engineering of systems and environments in which autonomous agents perform consequential work.

Why MAGE? Why Models?

One way to understand MAGE is as a classical software-engineering move: **add a level of indirection.**[^indirection] Conventional engineering has long separated the engineering of an artifact from its physical realization.

The origins of MAGE

MAGE grew out of an engineering problem I encountered while building DocAble, a service for making documents accessible to people with disabilities.

Who this book is for

This book is for software engineers who want to understand what changes when implementation can be delegated to capable agents.

What Makes Production Economical?

The engineering question is what useful delivery costs.

What Makes Progress Cumulative?

Choosing the least costly arrangement for the next change is not necessarily the best decision for the next hundred changes.

Lesson6.2-what-the-theory-predicts 6.2-what-the-theory-predicts

P1: Representation Leverage

**Trustworthy, task-relevant representations can reduce reconstruction and extend the work that humans and agents can complete at a given quality and resource budget.** They do so by exposing the distinctions and relationships needed for the task while suppressing implementation detail that would otherwise have to be reconstructed.

P2: Representation-Enabled Enforcement

**An explicit representation can make a selected obligation mechanically decidable, allowing Alignment to enforce it independently of the producing agent’s compliance.** Modeling supplies a form in which the property can be evaluated; Alignment supplies the mechanism that makes the result consequential.

P3: Governance Conversion and Engineering Capital

**When engineering judgment becomes trustworthy, reusable structure, later work can inherit productive capacity rather than purchase the same reasoning again.** Governance conversion is one route to this engineering capital.

P4: Governable Acceleration

**The effect of additional agentic capacity depends on the GEE through which it acts.** Where representations and assurance adequately support the work, added capacity can produce more durable progress without proportionate growth in human inspection.

Lesson7.4-the-engineer 7.4-the-engineer

Authority Follows Competence and Responsibility

MAGE increases both the leverage of engineering knowledge and the consequences of getting it wrong.

Professional authority

Engineering authority extends beyond technical capability.

The judgment frontier

One social purpose of the engineer is to be entrusted with, and answerable for, technical work too complex or consequential for ordinary individuals to undertake for themselves[cite: bugliarello-social-function].

Sign-Off Moves Toward Models and Evidence

In the factory Chapter 5 examined, the fleet constructed most of the implementation, maintained selected engineering representations, ran validators, and assembled evidence for the claims the design was supposed to satisfy.

From Full-Stack to Full-System Engineering

Software has used full-stack engineer to describe someone able to work across multiple implementation layers: interface, application logic, data, infrastructure, and deployment.

What Should We Teach?

If engineers increasingly review systems through representations and evidence rather than reconstructing every property from implementation, education should shift accordingly.

Is there software engineering knowledge you cannot just figure out for yourself?

The question for software engineering education is whether there is important software engineering knowledge that practitioners cannot reasonably be expected to figure out for themselves, or whether software engineering is distinct among the engineering disciplines in being predicated on adaptability more than specific expertise.

What shouldn't software engineers have to figure out for themselves?

I would concede some of this ground.

Shift the emphasis

Less educational effort may need to go toward producing routine implementation by hand, and more toward selecting abstractions, specifying properties, measuring systems, validating claims, reasoning about quality attributes, and governing autonomous work.

Change what students demonstrate

A capstone should therefore demonstrate more than a working artifact.

The Entry-Rung Problem

The traditional path into software engineering runs through implementation.
